messages:
alex: Hey team, customer on v2 streaming reports spikes of reconnects ~every 30s and when reconnecting clients get duplicated mid-stream chunks or a truncated final token. Logs attached from their session: trace=trace-9a8b7c.

maya: Oof. Any error codes? They seeing 4xx/5xx or just network resets?

alex: No 4xx. Client sees: \"net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET\" and in our edge logs we see connection closed by peer, then a new connect within <100ms. No auth failures.

ingrid: Streaming-bot attached metric snippet: 
```
# streaming-bot metrics excerpt
stream.connection.closed_by_peer{region=\"us-west-2\"} 24
stream.connects{region=\"us-west-2\"} 246
stream.bytes_sent 1.2e6
stream.last_chunk_interval_ms{p50}=28000
stream.last_chunk_interval_ms{p95}=31000
```
looks like periodic gaps ~30s.

sre-jen: That smells like an idle timeout somewhere + clients doing immediate reconnect loops (thundering reconnects). Could cause duplicate partials if resume token handling is racy.

maya: Customer sent a pcap and small reproduction using curl --no-buffer to our SSE endpoint. They included sequence of chunks: chunk N repeated on reconnect, then final chunk truncated. Pcap shows connection FIN from proxy then immediate new TCP handshake.

alex: repro steps they used (from customer):
1) curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.example/v2/stream?model=x' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
2) wait ~30s while partial tokens stream in small chunks
3) simulate flaky network by dropping packet (they used tc qdisc netem)
4) observe reconnect + duplicate chunk + sometimes truncated final token

ingrid: I pulled the edge proxy logs for trace-9a8b7c: upstream idle timeout=30s, keepalive_reaped=true, proxy emitted rst on client side.

sre-jen: Two hypotheses: (A) edge proxy idle timer set to 30s closes connection during quiet part between chunks; client reconnects quickly and requests resume; we accept resume but our prefix/KV cache race returns last chunk plus partial new chunk leading to duplication/truncation. (B) intermediate NAT/ALB is resetting and client reconnect storm overwhelms our resume de-dup path.

maya: Repro locally: I ran their curl with a proxy I control, set proxy idle timeout=15s, and forced packet drops. Observed identical behavior. I captured logs and small pcap.

alex: Immediate mitigation options suggested to customer: enable client-side exponential backoff on reconnect (avoid immediate retry), bump keepalive at reverse-proxy, and enable heartbeat comment frames e.g. every 10s.

ingrid: Long-term: make resume token application idempotent by returning an explicit resume offset + sequence id, and make KV cache retire shorter-lived flags to avoid replaying same chunk. Also add server-side detection for reconnect storms per session to queue/resume more safely.

sre-jen: Action items:
- maya: file internal bug with trace + pcap + repro steps, tag eng-runtime and eng-infra.
- alex: send customer quick mitigation steps (backoff + proxy keepalive) and request a small window to test.
- ingrid: start design doc for resume idempotency and resume offset protocol change.

maya: Filed bug RN-9842 with attachments and labeled P1. Link: https://redwood.internal/bugs/RN-9842

alex: Customer notified, applying proxy keepalive tweak in their staging. We'll follow up after their next test. :thumbsup:

streaming-bot: Deploy notice: routing-proxy/config updated by ops-ci at 2135680100, change: keepalive=60s (staging only).

sre-jen: Good. We'll monitor metrics and watch for decreased closed_by_peer count and smoother chunk intervals. I'll leave this thread open until post-test.
